name: Cryogenic dark/pinhole characterization of a Teledyne HAWAII-2RG (2048x2048 HgCdTe) infrared array held at 35 K in a closed-cycle test cryostat at ~10 microTorr
plain_name: Test a large infrared camera chip for a telescope while it is held at 35 K
description: Detector-head cooldowns of the SCALES H2RG imager and IFS arrays in the UCLA closed-cycle test cryostat: the detector is held at a constant 35 K (performance equivalent between 35 and 39 K) by a Lakeshore 336 controller, the cryostat interior is at ~10 microTorr, the head is cooled/warmed at 0.5 K/min, and dark frames and pinhole illumination (light source inside the cryostat) are read out through the SIDECAR ASIC/MACIE chain.
keywords: Test a large infrared camera chip for a telescope while it is held at 35 K

sources.citation: P. Benac, M. P. Fitzgerald, E. Wang et al., 'Laboratory testing and characterization of a hybrid fast/slow readout mode for the H2RG detectors in SCALES', arXiv:2508.21168 (2025)

requirements.rationale: The array is held at a constant 35 K during all cryogenic tests; the sample stage must reach and regulate at 35 K.
Optional: performance was equivalent anywhere from 35 to 39 K, so the full 35-39 K window is useful but not required.
The detector operates inside an evacuated cryostat (typical pressure ~10 microTorr).
Cryostat pressure during the tests was about 10 microTorr (1e-5 Torr); the machine must reach at least this vacuum to avoid condensation on the cold array.
The array is clocked and read out through 4 outputs via a cryogenic SIDECAR ASIC and a buffered cable to the warm MACIE card; cold-to-warm wiring feedthroughs are required.
Optional size gate: the array side is 2048 x 18 um = 36.864 mm, so the cold stage must clear at least that width (the packaged detector head is larger; its size is not stated).
Optional: the detector head was cooled and warmed under control at 0.5 K per minute.
Optional: the test cryostat used was a closed-cycle refrigerator system (no liquid cryogen).

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
